text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- President Jacques Chirac is expected tonight to announce a dissolution of the National Assembly and an early legislative election between May 25 and June 1, seen as necessary to implement further austerity measures and qualify for the first wave of European monetary union. Industry Minister Franck Borotra calls for further cuts in taxes and labour charges. Paris CAC-40 blue-chip stock index fell 2.59 percent on Friday on political uncertainty. (Les Echos, La Tribune, L'Agefi, Le Figaro, Liberation, The International Herald Tribune).
LES ECHOS
-- Credit Lyonnais near agreement with European authorities on rescue plan, which may entail the sale of most of its European subsidiaries, removing need for state recapitalisation.
-- EDF utility cuts prices by an average of 4.6 percent.
-- Poultry producer Doux seeks to set up activities in the USA and Brazil.
LA TRIBUNE
-- U.S. Warner to buy a 10 percent stake in CanalSatellite.
-- Small and medium-sized company heads less optimistic in April, survey shows.
L'AGEFI
-- Banque Hervet to be privatised before summer, according to Finance Minister Jean Arthuis.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- 53 percent of people polled by Sofres for Le Figaro favour a dissolution of the National Assembly.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Study says insurance companies made billions of francs of profit between 1992 and 1995 from re-insuring risk of natural disaster with state agencies.
-- Unions at TAT-Air Liberte to carry on strike.
-- SNCF railway operator to cut costs and re-consider partnership with catering supplier Servair to improve client service and cost management.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Voters gear for early legislative election campaign.
